killings.summary: Zeeshan (22), a Muslim carpenter from Amroha, was shot dead by police in a staged 'encounter' at a barricade in the Loni area of Ghaziabad.

Five religious structures, including a mosque and a mazar, removed for a road-widening project; internet services suspended and over 3,000 police deployed.
Mosque bulldozed as an alleged encroachment on village land.

~30 structures including three mosques and several mazars demolished over successive June drives; the Juna Kandla mosque, on the state Waqf register since 1965, razed at night. Residents said no notices were served and one drive proceeded despite a High Court stay.

City magistrate ordered the eviction and demolition of a ~70-year-old mosque inside the Collectorate compound and imposed retrospective damages of over Rs 64 million (~USD 745,000), on proceedings originating in a Bajrang Dal complaint.
Five buildings bulldozed in the Muslim-majority Begum Bagh locality for infrastructure serving the Mahakaleshwar temple corridor; around 90 buildings marked in the rolling clearance.

Port Authority demolished more than 100 homes in the dock area; police barricaded the area at 3 am, 14 residents faced criminal cases, and four-generation dock-worker families launched an indefinite sit-in.

House and office of an opposition Muslim municipal councillor demolished four days after a three-day show-cause notice—against the Supreme Court's mandated fifteen—over properties including the house where Nida Khan had stayed.

Western Railway clearance razed ~60% of the predominantly Muslim settlement within 48 hours—residents counted over 500 homes, plus shops and two mosques—days before Eid al-Adha, with no rehabilitation; the adjoining Dalit and Muslim settlement of Pampapura was demolished days later.

20 to 40 homes of Gujjar and Bakerwal families demolished in a forest-department eviction drive from around 5 am; residents said they were given no notice, and the territory's tribal affairs minister called it a 'targeted and cruel eviction'.

~100 homes in a minority-concentration settlement demolished in the presence of officials and police, after which no authority accepted responsibility; the High Court found the 'ghost demolition' prima facie without authority of law and five officials were suspended.

Walled compound owned by a Muslim municipal councillor demolished after a priest's murder, though he was not among the named accused and his role was merely 'being probed'; the accused was shot dead in an 'encounter'.
Demolition drive left ~310 families served flood-risk eviction notices scattered and in several cases homeless on the streets; older temples at the site were left standing.

After a cattle-slaughter case and a Hindutva highway blockade demanding action, the administration demolished structures and served notices on dozens of villagers; the High Court stayed the demolition of 38 houses, petitioners arguing demolition 'cannot become a form of collective punishment'.

Rampur Development Authority ordered the demolition of 38 of the 40 buildings of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, a Muslim-founded institution, as unauthorised construction; the order was stayed on 27 July pending appeal.

Family homes of two men identified by authorities as militants demolished with controlled explosives within a day of a policeman's killing, without judicial process; the homes belonged to their families, not to the accused.
Homes of two Muslim women demolished days after they were named as accused—not convicted—in a criminal case, citing 'illegal construction' on government land.
